name: Timor-Leste
snapshot: One of Asia's freest democracies, which became ASEAN's 11th member in 2025 but depends on a dwindling oil fund.
culture: Timor-Leste is overwhelmingly Catholic after Portuguese rule and the church's role in the resistance to Indonesian occupation. Tetum and Portuguese are official. Woven tais textiles and sacred houses, uma lulik, are central to clan identity. Independence leaders Xanana Gusmão and José Ramos-Horta still dominate politics.
society: Indonesia's occupation from 1975 to 1999 killed as many as a quarter of the population. Oil and gas revenue, saved in a sovereign fund, pays for most of the budget, but fields are running dry. Unemployment is high among a very young population. It ranks among Asia's leaders on press freedom.
situation: Xanana Gusmão returned as prime minister after his party won the 2023 election. José Ramos-Horta, a Nobel Peace laureate, has been president since 2022. The country formally joined ASEAN in October 2025. Student protests in 2025 forced lawmakers to drop plans to buy themselves new cars.
power: A semi-presidential republic. The prime minister leads the government with the confidence of the National Parliament; the directly elected president can veto laws and dissolve parliament.

sources.label: Tatoli: preparing to chair ASEAN in 2029

eat: Batar da'an, corn with pumpkin and beans

story: Portugal ruled Timor for 400 years. When it left in 1975, Indonesia invaded and its occupation killed perhaps a quarter of the population. In 1999 East Timorese voted for independence in a UN referendum, and Indonesian-backed militias burned the country. It became independent in 2002.
